title: German ZEW Sentiment Edges Up to 34.7, Eurozone Expectations Fall to 25.8
summary: Germany’s economic outlook showed a marked divergence in September between improving current conditions and largely unchanged expectations. The ZEW Indicator of Economic Sentiment edged from 34.2 to 34.7, falling well short of the 42.5 market forecast. By contrast, the Current Situation Index jumped from -61.1 to -47.1, beating expectations of -53.0. title: Euro: Downside pressure targets 1.1490 against US Dollar – UOB
summary: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang highlights renewed EUR/USD weakness after a sharper-than-expected drop below 1.1565 to 1.1522. He sees scope for a further test of 1.1520 intraday, with 1.1490 as the next key support over the coming weeks.

title: Brent: Higher risk premium and retest of highs – Rabobank
summary: Rabobank's Senior Energy Strategists Joe DeLaura and Florence Schmit revise their Brent outlook higher as Middle East disruptions tighten supply routes.

title: Bank of Japan: Gradual normalisation path outlined – Standard Chartered
summary: Standard Chartered’s Chong Hoon Park and Nicholas Chia expect the Bank of Japan to hike its policy rate by 25bps to 1.25% at the 17-18 September meeting.

title: Bank Of England: Jobs data supports steady policy – ING
summary: ING economist James Smith argues that recent United Kingdom (UK) jobs data underline a cooler labour market and weaker wage dynamics, reducing the risk of another inflation surge.
